statement: KybeDID and RootDID are person-grade, persona-agnostic credentials; personas are contextual bindings BENEATH that spine, never the other way round. Any code that needs a caller's constitutional principal must resolve it from the authenticated session's own auth_user_id via root_identity (person-grade, persona-agnostic), never by reading a persona-owned field that merely LOOKS like a DID (e.g. personas.root_did) and never by walking a persona cluster upward to infer personhood. Persona/auth_profile_id-scoped ownership may be used only as an authorization predicate on an ALREADY-resolved principal, never as the principal-resolution mechanism itself. A field's name is not evidence of its semantics — verify every write site before trusting a column as a sovereign identifier.
classification: Engineering/architectural invariant (candidate causal pattern) about identity-resolution direction — principal-first (KybeDID/RootDID -> Passport -> personas) vs persona-upward (persona -> guess a root -> infer personhood) — in the Passport/personhood identity layer.

occurrences.defect: A legacy Passport reconciliation capability resolved the principal by walking UP from a persona to its auth_profile_id cluster and matching personas.root_did against root_identity.did_uri. A same-day audit proved personas.root_did is a semantically overloaded legacy column — only one of at least eight write sites ever writes a genuine root_identity.did_uri into it; every other site writes a disposable, persona-level identifier (an FIO-handle DID, a hash of that handle, or an import placeholder). The heuristic therefore only worked by coincidence, for personas created through the one narrow write site that happened to bind correctly.

canaries.assertion: A persona whose OWN personas.root_did is a legacy 'did:fio:*' value (matching no root_identity.did_uri row) still gets its Passport's root_identity_id/kybe_identity_id reconciled successfully, because the resolved principal comes from the CALLER's auth_user_id, never from that field. A persona owned by a DIFFERENT auth_profile_id cluster cannot have its Passport rebound to the caller's principal — refused not_authorized, row left untouched.
resolveRootPrincipalForAuthUser resolves root_identity_id/kybe_id from auth_user_id alone and structurally never issues a query against the personas table (tablesTouched === ['root_identity']).

notes: SCHEMA DEBT RECORDED, NOT RESOLVED HERE: personas.root_did remains an overloaded legacy column with at least eight independent write sites producing at least four different semantic kinds of value (genuine RootDID, FIO-handle DID, hash-of-handle, import placeholder). Renaming it, migrating those write sites, or introducing a dedicated replacement FK (e.g. personas.bound_root_identity_id) is explicitly OUT OF SCOPE for the resolution this invariant derives from and is deferred to a separate identity-spine normalization task, per direct operator instruction (2026-08-15).

This invariant governs RESOLUTION DIRECTION, not the schema itself — it holds regardless of whether/when personas.root_did is eventually normalized, because the rule ('resolve principal from auth_user_id, use persona membership only for authorization') is correct independent of that column's later fate.

resolvePassportPrincipalForAuthUser and the newly extracted resolveRootPrincipalForAuthUser (services/identity/passportPrincipal.ts) were ALREADY the correct, ratified principal-first mechanism (PRD-PAG-001 Amendment A §A.3.1/§A.3.2, 2026-07-26) — this invariant does not introduce new architecture, it corrects a NEW capability that briefly deviated from already-ratified architecture, and generalizes the lesson so a future capability does not repeat the same deviation.
